messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: fixed optimx/minqa issue
parts:
Hi all,

I think I have figured out the optimx issue and why it was variable.

Basically:

1. The new 2018 version of "optimx" did not automatically install the package "minqa".  However, minqa was required for optimx ML searching with the "bobyqa" algorithm, which allows parameter searches with lower and upper bounds, and which is the algorithm that BioGeoBEARS-with-optimx was using.

2. For some reason, optimx does not report this problem, instead it just did one likelihood calculation, stopped the ML search after 1 step, and then returned NAs for the parameters

3. The NA parameters then caused a mysterious crash once the uppass calculations started.


Variability:

You wouldn't see this issue if you had the older optimx, or had minqa installed, or were using an optimizer other than optimx. (So, it would be most common on a "fresh install" of R and all packages)


The solutions:

1. I've put checks into BioGeoBEARS that check, if the 2018 version of optimx is being used, to check that minqa is installed. Also added a check for optimizers returning NA for parameters (in case there are future updates to the optimizer packages)

2. If you want to use optimx, you should do:

install.packages("minqa")

3. To get the code with the fix, do:

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github(repo="nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS")

...or...

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github(repo="nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS", INSTALL_opts="--byte-compile")

...if you want to try byte-compiling.

Cheers!
Nick
